title: Import endpoint leaks a reader on the failure path and hands scoped services to fire-and-forget work

consumerGuidance.architecture: ASP.NET Core Web API. IProductRepository is registered scoped and is backed by AppDbContext. The request scope is disposed when the response completes.
consumerGuidance.notes: Import files are supplied by authenticated tenant users and are not size-limited by the endpoint.

mustCite: the early return on an invalid header that skips disposal
the consequence of a retained file handle on every rejected upload
the correction of a using declaration or try/finally
the scoped IProductRepository captured by that work
the consequence that the repository and its DbContext are used after the request scope is disposed, and that failures are unobserved
a proportionate correction such as completing the work inside the request or handing it to a hosted queue with its own scope
that the row count comes from the uploaded file and is not bounded by the endpoint
the consequence of unbounded concurrent writes against the store
a proportionate correction such as batching or a bounded degree of parallelism

forbiddenFindings.example: Requiring ImportService to dispose the injected IProductRepository.
Requiring a background message broker or hosted service architecture rather than a bounded correction.
Objecting to the discard assignment syntax or to var.

notes: Three defects on one changed method: a manual resource with no owner on the failure path, work escaping the request scope, and unbounded fan-out over caller-controlled input.
